A greeting or a thanks gets a short reply when you mention @help, and only a reaction in #help when you don't. While it writes an answer, its avatar shows above the composer with three dots, like a person typing, and the dots go away when the answer lands. Helpers run on the Slirc server, so they work while your computer is off.

title: Bots
heading: Tip
text: Give each script its own bot. A password you can revoke on its own is easier to reason about than one account shared by four jobs.

title: Bots
heading: Polls: @poll
text: @poll runs polls in a channel. The quickest way to start one is the + next to the composer: choose Poll. Typing /poll on its own opens the same dialog. In the dialog, write the question and at least two options. Add gives you another row, up to ten. Drag an option by its handle to move it, or focus the handle and use the up and down arrow keys. Two switches set how people answer. Allow multiple answers lets each person pick more than one option. Anonymous hides who voted for what. Everyone still sees the counts and their own vote. Closes in ends the poll on its own after an hour, a day or a week. With None it stays open until someone closes it. Send posts the poll, and if @poll isn't in the channel yet it joins first. The poll shows as a card with the question and every option, each with a count and a bar. Tap an option to vote. Tap it again to take your vote back, or tap another option to change it. With multiple answers, each tap turns one option on or off. Counts update for everyone in the channel as votes come in. In a poll that isn't anonymous, the faces of the latest voters show next to each count. View votes opens the full list. It shows each option with its count and, unless the poll is anonymous, who voted and when. Your own vote shows as "You". In an anonymous poll Slirc never sends anyone's name to the app, so only the counts show. The person who started the poll, the channel's owner or an admin can close it from the ⋯ menu on the card. A closed poll shows the result with the winner marked, and nobody can vote anymore. You can also start a poll by typing it, with a question and at least two options separated by commas or by "or": @poll Lunch? pizza, sushi, salad @poll pizza or sushi? @poll Lunch? pizza, sushi for 1h @poll Lunch? pizza, sushi named /poll Lunch? pizza, sushi, salad does the same. Add for 30m, for 2h or for 1d to pick when it closes, from one minute up to 30 days. Without it, a typed poll closes a week after it started. Typed polls list voters only with named. Otherwise they work like anonymous ones. If a typed poll can't start, say it has only one option, Slirc doesn't post it. The New poll dialog opens with what you typed, at the part to fix. To vote by typing, use the number: @poll 2 or /poll 2. Your vote isn't posted in the channel. Slirc counts it and shows Counted: sushi as a notice only you see. Voting again moves your vote, or adds the option when the poll allows multiple answers. @poll results posts the running tally and @poll close closes the poll. Typed @poll close works for the person who started the poll or a channel op, and admins are ops in every channel. One poll is open per channel at a time. Starting a second one shows the open poll, which you close first. A poll has up to ten options, each under 80 characters, and a question under 200. Polls survive a restart, and one that came due while the server was down closes once the helper is back. @poll works in channels and groups it was added to, private ones included. It can't join DMs or threads. In a channel, start the line with @poll; a plain word "poll" is ordinary text. In your DM with poll, no @ is needed. From an IRC client, everything the helper posts is plain text, one line per option, and votes from there count on the card. The helper also posts the tally when a poll closes, which IRC clients read and Slirc leaves out because the card already shows it. A @poll 2 line you send in the channel is public there like any message, and the helper answers it with a private notice. To vote without anyone seeing, send it to the helper instead: /msg poll #lunch 2.

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
text: Same job, group chat on our own hardware. Very different footprint. Campfire is an excellent alternative: open source, self-hosted, runs one command, and you get the code. We measured both products side by side to see what the same job costs on our own hardware.

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: The numbers
text: metric Campfire Slirc RAM, idle 1.62 GB (76% of its own 2 GB cap) ~20 MB total (13.6 MB app + 6.6 MB Ergo) CPU, idle 2.03% ~0.1% processes 220 12 image size ~917 MB (877 MB app + 40 MB Redis) ~135 MB (97.8 MB app + 36.7 MB Ergo) extra services separate Redis container none

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: How it adds up
text: RAM: 81× CPU: ~20× processes: 18× disk images: 6.8×

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: Capacity
text: Campfire sits near its own 2 GiB cap before anyone connects. Slirc's whole stack uses about 1% of that, so the same cap holds roughly 80 Slirc stacks. Campfire alone eats 1.6 GB of its machine's 31 GB. Slirc's whole stack fits comfortably on its 3.8 GB host.

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: Load
text: Synthesized 250 concurrent IRC clients against the local Ergo instance: all registered and joined, then chattered at ~210 messages/s for 40 seconds, about 52k outbound deliveries after fanout. metric 250 users (measured) 500 users (modeled) Ergo RAM, idle 17 MiB 17 MiB Ergo RAM, during load 39 MiB 60-80 MiB Ergo CPU, sustained 5-15% of one core ~10-30% Ergo CPU, burst spike ~49% of one core under one core messages handled 8.4k in / 52k out ~2× This is the chatty worst case, every user talking continuously. Real groups sit mostly idle at the WebSocket relay, so actual capacity is well above the model.

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: Recommended server
text: Same ladder Campfire publishes (they start at 250 users / 2 GB / 1 CPU). Slirc's numbers start from the measured load above and scale for the whole stack, app relay, Ergo, Caddy, and headroom, not bare Ergo. Hetzner Cloud ARM servers hit these tiers out of the box, prices included. concurrent users RAM CPU Hetzner est. price 250 1 GB 1 CPU cax11 ~€7/mo 1,000 2 GB 2 CPU cax11 ~€7/mo 5,000 4 GB 4 CPU cax21 ~€13/mo 10,000 8 GB 8 CPU cax31 ~€25/mo Memory stays the cheap axis (Ergo idles at ~17 MiB and peaks under 40 MiB for 250 chatty users); the growth curve is CPU and the WebSocket fanout, which is why it climbs slower than Campfire's ladder. Personal agents add no server load. They run on your machine and connect as one more IRC client.

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: What Slirc does not have
text: Campfire and Slack both have server-side search. Slirc does not yet. Slack has voice and video; Slirc pastes a link. Matrix federates and encrypts end to end; Slirc does neither. This page is about what the same group chat costs to run, and the numbers only make sense next to that list.

title: Footprint: Slirc next to Campfire
heading: Method
text: Both hosts measured 2026-09-07 with podman stats (three samples, two seconds apart), podman images, and podman system df. Load numbers measured 2026-09-15 with a 250-client synthetic script against the local stack.

title: Run your own Slirc
text: Self-host Slirc on a fresh Linux server with one command. Three containers run on a private Docker network: Caddy handles HTTPS, Bun serves the app, and Ergo runs IRC underneath. The Elastic License 2.0 lets you run Slirc for your own group. Hosting it for others requires permission from the author.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: What you need
text: A Linux server (x86_64 or arm64). A 2 vCPU, 4 GB box runs Slirc with room to spare. A domain with an A or AAAA DNS record pointed at the server, and ports 80 and 443 reachable from the internet. Optional API keys (all skippable during setup and easy to add later via slirc env): Resend for sign-in emails and invites, GIPHY for /giphy search, and OpenRouter for AI answers in @help and natural-language @remind.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Run the installer
text: SSH into your server and run: curl -fsSL https://install.slirc.org | sudo bash You can also fetch the script straight from GitHub (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitbonsai/slirc/main/install.sh). The installer installs Docker Engine and the Compose plugin if they are missing, asks four short questions, generates every secret and config file, pulls the multi-arch images (ghcr.io/bitbonsai/slirc:latest, ghcr.io/bitbonsai/slirc-ergo:v2.19.1, and caddy:2-alpine), starts the stack, and enables nightly updates: Domain: checks that DNS resolves to the server (warns if not, and lets you continue anyway). Owner email and nickname: creates the initial admin account. Workspace mode and default channel: private workspace (invite-only #general, default) or public peek (visitors can read your default public channel such as #general or #feedback and sign up). Optional integrations, direct IRC, and updates: press Enter to skip any of Resend (RESEND_API_KEY + RESEND_FROM), GIPHY (GIPHY_API_KEY), and OpenRouter (OPENROUTER_API_KEY + @help model, default anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5). Then pick whether to expose direct IRC TLS on port 6697 (default loopback only) and whether to keep nightly automatic updates on (default yes).

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: What gets installed
text: /opt/slirc/: compose.yaml, .env, app.env (mode 0600), Caddyfile, ergo.yaml (mode 0600), and ergo.motd. /var/lib/slirc/: persistent app SQLite database and uploads (app/), Ergo account and history databases (ergo/), Caddy certificates (caddy/), and backup archives (backups/). /var/lib/slirc-keys/irc-key: 32 random bytes (mode 0600) that derive every IRC password via HMAC. It stays outside /var/lib/slirc so backups never hold anything that logs in to IRC. Copy it into your password manager once, separately from backups, and never replace it while people use the server. /usr/local/bin/slirc: management CLI for status, logs, restarts, updates, backups, and env edits. slirc-update.timer (systemd, or /etc/cron.daily/slirc-auto-update): checks nightly around 03:30 for new container images. Re-running the installer is safe: existing keys, databases, app.env, and ergo.yaml are preserved.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: First sign-in
text: If you entered a Resend key: open https://yourdomain, enter your owner email, and sign in with the 6-digit code or link Resend delivers. If you skipped Resend: run slirc login-link on the server to print a one-time 15-minute sign-in link for the owner account. When you are ready for email sign-ins and team invitations, run slirc env, uncomment RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM, and save. Your owner account is an admin and can create channels and invite people. In private_workspace mode, other people join by invitation. In public_playground mode, visitors can read your default public channel (such as #general or #feedback) and sign up from the sign-in form while the day's mail count stays under MAIL_DAILY_LIMIT (SIGNUP_DOMAIN_LIMIT, default 30, caps new signups per receiving domain per hour). See Getting started.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Automatic updates and safe restarts
text: Like ONCE, a self-hosted Slirc instance checks for new images once every 24 hours via slirc-update.timer (slirc update --auto): When no image digest has changed, nothing restarts. When only the slirc app image has changed, slirc update recreates only the slirc container (--no-deps), leaving Ergo running so IRC sessions stay connected. Caddy retries in-flight HTTP requests for up to 20 seconds while the new container comes up. After swapping in the new app container, slirc update polls /healthz. If the new image fails health checks within 60 seconds, it rolls back automatically to the previous healthy image ID. Superseded untagged layers are pruned after a clean update so disk usage stays flat. Turn nightly updates off or check the next scheduled run at any time: slirc auto-update status slirc auto-update off slirc auto-update on

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Day-to-day management
text: slirc elevates automatically with sudo when run as a non-root user so secrets under /opt/slirc stay mode 0600. slirc status # containers, /healthz, version, updates, and paths slirc logs [service] # follow logs (slirc, ergo, caddy, or all) slirc restart [service] # restart app without dropping Ergo (or --all) slirc update # pull images, recreate changed services, rollback on failure slirc auto-update status # inspect or toggle nightly automatic updates slirc backup [dest] # create a consistent tar.gz backup (excludes irc-key) slirc env [--compose] # edit app.env (or .env with --compose) and recreate slirc login-link [nick] # mint a one-time 15-minute sign-in link on the server slirc sync-certs # sync Caddy's TLS cert to Ergo (for public :6697) slirc uninstall # stop and remove Slirc (asks before deleting data) slirc backup takes transactionally consistent SQLite snapshots (chat.sqlite and ergo_history.db), verifies them with PRAGMA integrity_check, includes ircd.db, avatars, and config, and leaves /var/lib/slirc-keys/irc-key out of the archive. Copy archives off the server on a schedule. To restore a backup on a new server, place your saved irc-key at /var/lib/slirc-keys/irc-key (mode 0600), stop the stack, extract config/* to /opt/slirc/, app/* to /var/lib/slirc/app/, and ergo/* to /var/lib/slirc/ergo/, remove any leftover -wal/-shm files, and start the stack again with docker compose --project-directory /opt/slirc -f /opt/slirc/compose.yaml up -d. If you enabled direct IRC TLS on port 6697, the installer sets SLIRC_IRC_HOST in app.env so the in-app IRC clients tab fills in your server address, and adds /etc/cron.daily/slirc-sync-certs so renewed Let's Encrypt certificates reload into Ergo via SIGHUP without dropping connections. To turn :6697 on later, set ERGO_TLS_BIND=0.0.0.0 via slirc env --compose, uncomment SLIRC_IRC_HOST via slirc env, and run slirc sync-certs.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Non-interactive and automated installs
text: Pass flags (or matching SLIRC_* environment variables) for scripted or CI installs: curl -fsSL https://install.slirc.org | sudo bash -s -- \ --non-interactive \ --domain chat.example.com \ --owner-email you@example.com \ --owner-nick you \ --mode public \ --channel feedback \ --resend-api-key re_... \ --resend-from 'Slirc <slirc@chat.example.com>' \ --giphy-api-key ... \ --openrouter-api-key ... \ --help-model anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 Add --expose-irc to publish port 6697 on 0.0.0.0, --no-auto-update to disable nightly updates, --skip-dns-check to skip the DNS lookup, or --dry-run to render configuration into temporary directories without installing Docker or starting containers.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Optional environment variables
text: Add or change any of these in /opt/slirc/app.env using slirc env (or ~/.config/slirc/env in manual setups). Because Docker and Podman read env files only when a container is created, recreate the app container after any edit (slirc env does this automatically). GIPHY_API_KEY: enables GIPHY search and the welcome helper's daily greeting gif in your public channel. OPENROUTER_API_KEY: enables the help bot and natural-language reminders through OpenRouter. Model names are OpenRouter ids; older bare names such as mimo-v2.5 still work. HELP_ANSWER_MODEL: model that writes help answers (default anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5). HELP_CLASSIFIER_MODEL: cheaper model that first sorts each message into a Slirc question, small talk, or off topic (default xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash). TYPESAFE_API_KEY: sorts messages with TypeSafe's Jev instead (classifier defaults to jev-latest; TYPESAFE_BASE_URL and TYPESAFE_INPUT_PRICE_PER_BILLION are optional). HELP_MODEL: model for reminders and other helpers (default xiaomi/mimo-v2.5). SLIRC_HELPER_DAILY_LIMIT: caps model calls that the help bot and natural-language reminders make for one account in 24 hours, combined (default 100). Past the limit, help asks you to try again tomorrow and reminders still accept short forms such as in 20m stretch, tomorrow 9:00 pick up cake, list, and cancel 3. SLIRC_HELPERS: comma list of helpers to run, such as help,remind. Unset runs help, remind, poll, and welcome; links runs only when listed; an unknown name stops the app at start. Set SLIRC_HELPERS_ENABLED=false to run none. SLIRC_AGENTS_ENABLED=false: turns off coding-agent pairing on the instance. OPEN_CHAT_ROOM: sets which public channel signed-out visitors can peek at in public_playground mode (default #open-chat, for example #feedback). SLIRC_BRAND: optional brand override (slirc.app for the blue hosted lockup); unset uses the neutral Slirc mark. SLIRC_EMOJI_BUDGET_BYTES: caps total custom emoji storage in bytes (default 104857600, 100 MB); each member can add 50 custom emoji per 24 hours. TESTFLIGHT_URL: public iPhone TestFlight link in the form https://testflight.apple.com/join/<code>. Signed-in, verified members see Get the iPhone app in More on a phone and in Devices -> Add your phone on desktop. Unset, or any other URL, hides it. MAIL_DAILY_WARN (default 80) and MAIL_DAILY_LIMIT (default 100): logs a warning and caps daily Resend volume for the instance. Bulk email invites stop at 75% of MAIL_DAILY_LIMIT so sign-in emails keep going through. When several instances share one Resend key, split the account's daily limit between them. Run bun scripts/mail-count.ts in the app container to print today, the last 7 days, and the month so far.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: History retention
text: The supplied Ergo config uses history.restrictions.expire-time: 0s: persistent messages stay stored until someone explicitly deletes them. Existing installations must update their mounted ergo.yaml separately; changing the example file does not alter a running server. Ergo applies this setting on SIGHUP without restarting. Disabling expiry does not restore messages purged under an earlier policy. Monitor disk usage and keep backups.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Advanced / manual setup (rootless Podman, host Caddy, and just)
text: If you prefer rootless Podman, host-level Caddy, and source builds pushed from your own machine with just, the repo keeps its original two-container Compose files untouched under deploy/.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: Prerequisites
text: A Linux server with rootless Podman, podman-compose, Git, and just. The Ergo image ghcr.io/bitbonsai/slirc-ergo:v2.19.1 ships for ARM64 and x86_64 under one tag. A domain pointed at the server and Caddy on the host for TLS. Your own machine with Git and just for deploys. Deploys push a committed tree and reset the server checkout to that exact commit.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: 1. Clone and set your host
text: On your machine: git clone https://github.com/bitbonsai/slirc cd slirc Open justfile and set the SSH host, checkout path, and config directory at the top to your own values.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: 2. Config on the server
text: Keep secrets outside git in ~/.config/slirc (mode 0700), with env and ergo.yaml at mode 0600: ssh yourserver mkdir -p ~/.config/slirc && chmod 700 ~/.config/slirc Create ~/.config/slirc/env: APP_HOST=app.yourdomain APP_ORIGIN=https://app.yourdomain OWNER_NICK=yournick USERS_JSON={"yournick":"you@example.com"} ERGO_OPER_USER=slirc-org ERGO_OPER_PASS=another-long-random-password SLIRC_MODE=private_workspace IRC_CHANNEL=#general OPEN_CHANNELS= SLIRC_TRUSTED_PROXIES=10.89.0.14 RESEND_API_KEY=re_... RESEND_FROM=Slirc <slirc@yourdomain> VAPID_CONTACT=mailto:you@example.com Create the 32-byte IRC password key outside ~/.config/slirc and copy it to your password manager: mkdir -p ~/.config/slirc-keys/org && chmod 700 ~/.config/slirc-keys openssl rand -out ~/.config/slirc-keys/org/irc-key 32 && chmod 600 ~/.config/slirc-keys/org/irc-key Copy ergo/ergo.example.yaml to ~/.config/slirc/ergo.yaml: scp ergo/ergo.example.yaml yourserver:~/.config/slirc/ergo.yaml Edit network.name and server.name to your domain, ensure channels.operator-only-creation: true and ip-limits.exempted covers 10.0.0.0/8, and replace the slirc-org oper password hash using: podman run --rm -it ghcr.io/bitbonsai/slirc-ergo:v2.19.1 ergo genpasswd

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: 3. Host Caddy
text: Copy caddy/example.caddy to your Caddy sites directory and replace the domain and paths with yours. The app block forwards each visitor's IP cleanly: app.yourdomain { handle { reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:9010 { lb_try_duration 20s header_up X-Forwarded-For {client_ip} } } } Port 9010 binds to localhost only. Browsers reach IRC through the app's /irc relay, so Ergo needs no WebSocket listener. Reload Caddy.

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: 4. Bootstrap and deploy
text: Back on your machine, with a clean tree: just bootstrap just status just logs app Day to day: just deploy # tests, then rebuild and recreate the app; Ergo keeps running just deploy-ergo # recreate Ergo; the app keeps running just deploy-docs # publish the docs site, if you serve one just logs ergo Before upgrading manually, rehearse app schema migrations on a consistent snapshot: cd app bun scripts/rehearse-migration.ts /private/backups/app.sqlite

title: Run your own Slirc
heading: When something is off
text: "Reconnecting..." in the browser after a burst of joins. The container network subnet is missing from ip-limits.exempted in ergo.yaml. Add it and reload Ergo with SIGHUP. owner credentials are missing on start. OWNER_NICK is missing as a key in USERS_JSON. IRC key file /run/slirc-irc-key is missing on start. Restore or create the 32-byte key file at /var/lib/slirc-keys/irc-key (or SLIRC_IRC_KEY_PATH in manual setups). Sign-in links never arrive. Check RESEND_FROM is a verified sender on your Resend account, then run slirc logs slirc (or just logs app) for the send error. You can always sign in as the owner with slirc login-link. Caddy fails to issue a certificate. Confirm your domain's A/AAAA record resolves to the server and ports 80 and 443 are open in your firewall (ufw or cloud security group), then check slirc logs caddy. Ergo logs read ircd.yaml: is a directory. ergo.yaml was missing when the container started and the bind mount created a directory in its place. Remove that directory, restore ergo.yaml, and recreate Ergo.

title: FAQ
text: The questions people bring first, answered in a paragraph each. The linked guides carry the detail.

title: FAQ
heading: Is it free?
text: Running your own Slirc instance is free under the Elastic License 2.0. You can use it, change it, and host it for your own group. The license reserves offering Slirc to others as a hosted service, and it stays under the Elastic License 2.0 permanently.

title: FAQ
heading: Do I need to know IRC?
text: No. The app uses channels, people, and messages. IRC shows up only if you open a terminal client, and then everything still makes sense.

title: FAQ
heading: Can I use my existing IRC client?
text: Yes. Halloy, Senpai, WeeChat, Textual, and Revolution IRC are documented. Password or client certificate.

title: FAQ
heading: When can I use an agent?
text: Pi, Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode work today. Copy the first line from the Agents page, such as npx slirc-agent@latest chat.example.com, and run it in a terminal or in a running Pi, Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode session. Then press Allow in Slirc. See Agents.

title: FAQ
heading: Who can tell my agent what to do?
text: Only messages from your own account, checked by the IRC account tag. Other people's mentions are ignored.

title: FAQ
heading: Is deleting a message permanent?
text: Deleting removes it from server history. An IRC client that already received it may keep a copy. The privacy page says this plainly.

title: FAQ
heading: Does it do push notifications on iPhone?
text: Yes, from Slirc saved to the Home Screen from Safari. Safari only sends web push to Home Screen apps. The iPhone app in TestFlight has no notifications yet; Download has both.

title: FAQ
heading: How big can a group get?
text: Anywhere from two people to a few hundred. One €7 ARM server carried 250 concurrent chatty users in our load test with Ergo under 40 MiB, and the hosting ladder goes to 5,000 online. Features are added when regular use asks for them.

title: FAQ
heading: Why IRC?
text: See About. Short version: IRC is small and open, it has decades of clients, and it keeps every feature honest.

title: FAQ
heading: Can I move away later?
text: Yes. Ergo's history database and the app's SQLite file are yours. Any IRC client reads the history today.

title: Design system
text: The current app uses Catppuccin Mocha and Latte, with Slirc lime in both. This reference documents shipped styles and their source files.

title: Design system
heading: Source files
text: The app shell is assembled from app/partials/*.html into app/public/index.html (generated; never edit directly). Alpine components live in app/client/ and ship as /client.js. Shared tokens and component styles are in app/public/style.css; the shell partials also carry effective style overrides. app/public/theme.js applies the appearance preference before CSS and first paint. Examples and tables on this page are hand-written. The page links /style.css, so previews pick up real style changes, but its prose and markup stay as written. Edit this page when a component changes.

title: Design system
heading: Appearance
text: Settings → Appearance offers System, Light, and Dark. System is the default and follows the device preference live; an explicit choice overrides it. The choice saves to your account and follows you across devices on their next load. localStorage under slirc-theme supplies the first paint and signed-out pages; after sign-in, the account preference takes over. Changes apply immediately. Failed saves keep the local choice without an error dialog. Blocked storage still allows changes on the current page. Invalid or missing preferences use System. theme.js sets data-theme and data-theme-preference on <html>, native color-scheme, and the browser theme color before the stylesheet loads. Theme selection must not wait for sign-in or Alpine. Preview themeDarkLight Doesn't change your settings. Dark CanvasPanelTextFillAccentLinksDanger Light CanvasPanelTextFillAccentLinksDanger

title: Design system
heading: Color and surfaces
text: Dark uses Catppuccin Mocha; light uses Latte neutrals and Slirc lime. Brand fill and accent ink are separate tokens. Pastel lime reads well as a fill under dark text and poorly as small text on a light canvas. Keep lime under roughly ten percent of a typical screen. title: Design system
heading: Typography, spacing, and layout
text: New and edited components use the shared tokens in app/public/style.css instead of literal values; existing components migrate when touched. A literal needs a concrete layout or accessibility reason.

title: Design system
heading: Fonts
text: Slirc loads no webfont, so JetBrains Mono shows only where it is installed. On desktop, nicks switch to the system font. Token Stack Use --ui system-ui -apple-system BlinkMacSystemFont "Segoe UI" sans-serif Chrome, headings, buttons, menus, cards. --mono "JetBrains Mono" ui-monospace "Cascadia Code" "SFMono-Regular" Menlo monospace Messages, composer, code, fences. Line height is 1.45 for UI body and about 1.55 for messages. Conversation intros (channel-intro, such as the top of Notes or a new channel) sit in the message column but use --ui.

title: Design system
heading: Type
text: Six steps, with no 13px step on purpose. The metadata floor is --text-xs (12px); only badge counts go down to --text-2xs (11px). Token rem px Use --text-2xs .6875rem 11px Badges and counts. --text-xs .75rem 12px Timestamps, hints, status, tooltips. --text-sm .875rem 14px UI body, inputs, menus, button labels. --text-base 1rem 16px Messages. --text-lg 1.25rem 20px Sheet and dialog heads. --text-xl 1.5rem 24px Page and display heads. Tooltips, hints, and status use --text-xs (12px); button labels use --text-sm (14px). Exceptions: glyphs sized to a fixed container (avatar initials, badge digits), display sizes of 1.75rem and 2rem, and em sizes inside code. In light, timestamps drop to a lighter weight and keep full opacity.

title: Design system
heading: Spacing
text: Gaps and padding step through six values. Pick the smallest step that separates two groups; skip a step to mark a new group. Token rem px Use --space-1 .25rem 4px Icon to label, chip padding. --space-2 .5rem 8px Control gaps and padding. --space-3 .75rem 12px Compact panels, menu padding. --space-4 1rem 16px Standard panels and cards. --space-5 1.5rem 24px Section gaps, dialog padding. --space-6 2rem 32px Large separation between page groups. Use rem for type, gaps, padding, and radii; px for 1–2px borders and focus outlines. Touch targets stay at least 2.75rem (44px at the default root size); safe-area insets add on top.

title: Design system
heading: Radius
text: Radius grows with the surface, and a nested surface uses a smaller radius than its container. Token Value Use --radius-xs .25rem Code chips, tiny marks. --radius-sm .4rem Chips, copy buttons. --radius-md .55rem Buttons, inputs, menu items. --radius-lg .75rem Menus, popovers, cards. --radius-xl 1rem Dialogs, toasts. --radius-pill 999px Pills, badges, composer. --radius-round 50% Avatars and circular buttons.

title: Design system
heading: Motion
text: Every transition uses --ease-standard, cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). Loops such as spinners and pulses keep their own durations. Token Duration Use --dur-micro .1s Hover color and opacity. --dur-fast .15s Menus, dialogs, toggles. --dur-base .2s Sheets, slides, toasts. --dur-entrance .3s Message entrance. --dur-reveal .5s Banners and boot.

title: Design system
heading: Shadows
text: Elevation has three steps. Dark uses black alphas strong enough to lift glass off the canvas; light uses var(--shadow) (#4c4f691a), a Latte text tint that stays quiet on pale surfaces. Token Dark Light Use --shadow-sm 0 .3rem .9rem #0006 0 .2rem .6rem var(--shadow) Typing row, chips, inline popovers. --shadow-md 0 .5rem 1.5rem #0009 0 .5rem 1.5rem var(--shadow) Menus, tooltips, link popover, new-below pill. --shadow-lg 0 1.5rem 5rem #000b 0 1rem 3rem var(--shadow) Command palette, header DM list, dialogs.

heading: State fills
text: Light needs solid Latte fills where dark can use brand alphas. Token Dark Light Use --active-fill Brand at 13% #d9eddc Active channel or DM row. --active-ring transparent #2377192e Inset 1px border on the active row. --mention-me-fill Link teal at 22% #b8e7b6 Mentions of you. --avatar-fill var(--panel-hi) #ccd0da Avatar fallback behind initials and photos.

title: Design system
heading: Disabled
text: Disabled controls fade and keep their layout and label. Busy is a separate state that hides the label behind a ring and keeps the control's size. Token Value Use --disabled-opacity .5 Disabled buttons, inputs, and menu items in both themes.

title: Design system
heading: Layout
text: Desktop has a far-left workspace rail (when signed in with saved workspaces), a 15rem conversation rail, and an 860px maximum message column. Channels in the sidebar support desktop drag-to-reorder with a 30% opacity floating ghost row, plus Alt+Up/Down keyboard reordering. Phone layout checks for a coarse pointer as well as the width. Header height is calc(3.625rem + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)). Phone navigation is --nav-h: 3.75rem, lifted by --nav-lift (the home-indicator inset less .75rem, at least .5rem), and phone screens pad their bottom by both so content clears the tab bar. --composer-space is measured at runtime by app/client/composer-editor.ts, with CSS fallbacks before measurement.

text: Use the same lime mark in both themes. Light surfaces need dark lettering, dark surfaces white lettering. Preserve aspect ratio; do not invert the whole lockup. Informative logos get Slirc alt text; decorative marks beside visible branding get empty alt text. Dark surface Light surface The mark is the speech bubble from the slirc.org lockup, with a green-to-blue gradient that stays the same in both themes. bun scripts/build-icons.ts renders every logo file below from scripts/icons/app-icon.svg; the light files take the mark from brand-org-light.svg. Dark has white lettering, light has #11111B. PNGs at 1x and @2x sit beside each for emails. brand-app-dark.svg, brand-app-light.svg slirc.app lockup with the solid blue mark, used when SLIRC_BRAND=slirc.app is set (hosted workspaces); self-hosted private workspaces use the neutral Slirc mark by default. The server sets data-brand on the shell and style.css swaps the lockup by brand and theme. logo-light.webp Light mark, from brand-org-light.svg. Light theme swaps it in with content: url(). icons/slirc-light.svg Light service bot mark, the light mark cropped to its outline. icons/ui/nav-{home,dms}-light.svg Light mobile nav Home and DMs icons. Home is the light mark. Monochrome nav icons keep the darkening filter. icons/bots/*-light.svg Helper bot marks in pastel Latte for light: help #5fd27c, remind #fb9a62, poll #b48af4, updates #e9b949. Dark keeps the Mocha data-URI marks.

title: Design system
heading: Icons
text: UI controls use Lucide, distributed under the ISC licence. The curated local sprite is app/public/icons/lucide/sprite.svg; lucideIcon() in app/client/presentation.ts emits trusted SVG markup. A name is usable only when its symbol exists in the sprite; missing names render empty. 24×24 viewBox, 2px stroke, round caps/joins, currentColor. Icon-only buttons need an accessible label; their SVG is decorative. Use Lucide for new controls. Don't use text glyphs or emoji in place of control icons.

title: Design system
heading: Glass, layering, and motion
text: --blur-light is blur(3px), --blur-medium blur(9px), --blur-heavy blur(18px). Glass pairs blur with a panel tint for text contrast. Floating glass surfaces share one tint, --glass-tint (panel at 74%), and --glass-filter. In dark the filter blurs and darkens what is behind (saturate(1.2) brightness(.75)) so a panel always sits below the content it covers; light only blurs and uses quieter shadows. Fixed chrome (header, docked rooms rail, members panel, composer, mobile nav) shares --glass-chrome (panel at 60%); dialogs stay near-solid at 96%. An element with a backdrop-filter, or with a filter or opacity below 1, is a backdrop root. A blurred child inside it blurs nothing and the content behind shows through sharp. So a glass menu that opens from a blurred surface renders outside it. The composer + menu (composer-plus-menu) is teleported to the end of body with x-teleport and fixed at --z-floating. placePlusMenu in app/client/popups.ts sets its left edge on the + button and its bottom just above the composer, and places it again on resize and when the phone keyboard moves the composer. When blur fails to reach the content behind a panel, look for a backdrop root among its ancestors. The overlay ladder lives in a second :root block: content 1, header 20, navigation menus 90/91, dialog 100, boot screen 102, --z-tooltip 120. Native dialogs use the browser top layer. Motion tokens are under Typography, spacing, and layout. Component durations: --dur-boot-pop 450ms, --dur-boot-exit 150ms, --dur-reaction 380ms; dialogs use --dur-fast. Boot and reaction animations play once. Reduced motion removes nonessential entrances and transitions. Shared CSS still carries view-transition and arrival rules that the current shell disables. Document what the shell does and leave the dormant rules out.

title: Design system
heading: Buttons and loading
text: Save changesCancelDeleteDisabledSaveResend SendDelete Loading agents… Shared button classes: btn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-danger, link-button. Resting buttons have no borders. Busy (.busy with aria-busy) hides the label and shows a ring in the button's ink, so it keeps its width; disabled stays distinct; keyboard focus has an explicit full-strength outline. A standalone spinner leads a loading line in profile-note loading. Some controls have classes of their own.

title: Design system
heading: Native forms and notifications
text: Display name AppearanceSystemLightDark Syncs with your account. Could not save. Try again. Confirm resend NotificationsOnChange Native inputs, selects, and checkboxes use the effective color scheme. form-fields spaces fields; form-field groups a control with its hint. form-error pairs a tinted error surface with a decorative icon. form-consent keeps a native checkbox beside its label in a bordered row. Input borders stay quiet until focus; modal forms focus their first useful field. settings-toggle is a labelled switch; prefs-toggle is a disclosure. Appearance uses a native select.

title: Design system
heading: Dialog
text: Delete channel? Deleting #design removes its threads and history for everyone. CancelDelete Real modal markup is <dialog class="custom-modal"> with a notice-card or form card; only the card is shown here, and its h2 title is shown as plain text so it stays out of this page's contents. Native top-layer dialogs cancel on Escape, trap Tab among visible enabled controls, and restore the invoker. A destructive confirmation opens with focus on Cancel. Never use alert, confirm or prompt.

heading: Cards and notices
text: Invitation Join Slirc Pick a display name and you're in. No password. Display name Join Slirc Invitation and admission pages use profile-dialog-card profile-screen-card admission-card: an invite-heading with join-eyebrow, join-heading, and join-note, then the form and admission-actions. The real heading is an h1. Check your email We sent a sign-in link to ada@example.com. Use another email notice-card is the centered informational card: optional notice-icon, title, muted copy, then pair-actions. delete-confirmation left-aligns it for destructive dialogs. Could not reach the server. Retrying… notify-banner is the transcript banner for errors and connection notes; it sticks to the top of the messages. notify-banner-close adds a dismiss. Connection and delivery errors go here. Command and input feedback, like an unknown command or a missing argument, goes to an auto toast. No invitations yet. Invite someone from a channel or by email. Could not load invitations. Retry Empty states use a compact informative notice: a subtle bordered panel with muted copy (invitation-empty), or a light danger tint with its Retry inside for a load failure (invitation-notice-error). Neither has a stripe, divider or illustration. When agents are off for the instance, the Agents page opens with agents-off, a bordered panel that says what agents are and who can turn them on, with the command or link to do it.

Uncertain asks for consent first, since a resend may duplicate.

title: Design system
heading: Composer
text: Send is a lime circle with a dark glyph in both themes; + is a muted glyph with no fill. Phone hits are at least 44px. On phone the composer is a pill that grows into a card for multiline drafts. On desktop, the Mac app included, it is an 18px rounded rectangle with --radius-lg + and Send set concentric inside it. + attaches photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP, up to 12 MB) and videos (MP4, MOV, WebM). With polls on, it opens a menu with Photo or video and Poll. While files upload, the chips dim under a spinner and the status line is for screen readers only. Where the browser has WebCodecs, app/client/video-compress.ts re-encodes a picked or dropped MP4 or MOV on the device before it stages: H.264 at about 720p (long edge 1280), 2.5 Mbps, at most 30 fps. The encoder is its own bundle, /video-encode.js, loaded only when someone picks a video. A clip that already fits 720p and is under 4 MB or near the target bitrate goes up as picked, and so does any clip whose result would not be smaller. With compression available a pick can be up to 500 MB; the file that uploads must still be under 30 MB. While it compresses, the clip shows as media-chip compressing: the preview at 50% with its percent in media-progress (--text-2xs mono, tabular digits) and × to cancel. The screen-reader status says Compressing… in 10% steps. Send stays disabled until it finishes, and a second pick meanwhile is refused with a note. When a reply thread is docked beside the channel on desktop, only the focused composer keeps the brand border and lime Send; the other turns to --secondary-fill with muted ink until it takes focus, and with neither focused the thread composer counts as active. Opening a conversation must not open the phone keyboard. Autocomplete, Markdown shortcuts, pending uploads, and edit state belong to the composer feature; Cmd/Ctrl+B, Cmd/Ctrl+I, and Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+C wrap the selection or caret word in Markdown.

title: Design system
heading: Composer states

title: Design system
heading: Tooltips and toast
text: 👍3Ada, Ben, and you Channel link copied Reminder: stretchOpenDismiss Generic slirc-tooltip lives in the shell partial and opens on hover and keyboard focus. reaction-tooltip and thread-tooltip remain separate variants. The shared tooltip uses a low-alpha panel tint for text contrast. glass-toast pills sit above the composer in toast-region and come in two kinds. Auto (the default, note) confirms something that just happened, or answers a command or input the app could not take; it shows even while the banner is up. A lighter layer drains toward the dismiss button over 5s, plus 1s per 30 characters of text up to 9s, and the toast closes when it empties; hover or keyboard focus pauses it. With reduced motion the layer stays still and the toast still closes on time. A newer auto toast replaces the current one. Sticky (glass-toast sticky, sticky) is for something that needs the person, like a reminder that fired while they were elsewhere. It has no timer. It uses the same glass as other toasts, with a bell, a toast-action button and a quiet Dismiss, and it stays until one is chosen. It fades in once over 160ms, without movement under reduced motion, and never flashes. Its state is separate, so an auto toast never replaces or pushes it away; when both show, sticky sits above auto. Several sticky toasts stack newest first, up to three; after that one row says how many more wait, with Open and Dismiss all. Open goes to the conversation and clears every toast for it. Toasts live in the app shell, so they show on every screen: above the composer in a conversation, at the bottom of the screen (above the phone nav) elsewhere.

heading: Mobile
text: ben09:42 👍❤️😂🔥👀 EditReply in threadRemind meDelete Long press on phone opens action-sheet in dialog.custom-modal.sheet-modal, over sheet-backdrop (dim plus light blur). sheet-head names the message, sheet-reactions holds quick reactions and Add reaction, sheet-actions mirrors the message menu. Back or Escape returns to the actions; a pick reacts and closes the sheet. The sheet rides above the keyboard while the field has focus. HomeDMsMoreNew messages below mobile-nav is the glass pill fixed low on phone screens, inside the home-indicator inset the way iOS tab bars sit. It holds Home, DMs, and More, with nav-dot for unread. The pill is --nav-surface (--panel-hi at 28% in dark, white at 45% in light) under a light blur, with no border. The active tab gets a --nav-active pill a small step lighter than the bar and a white label; the other tabs sit at 60%. It shows on the tab screens and the pages under More, and hides inside conversations and while the keyboard is open. new-below floats above the composer when new messages arrive out of view; tap to jump down. Both are fixed in the app and shown in flow here. The More tab stacks three more-card groups (--panel-hi at 55%, --radius-lg) at the bottom, near the tab bar. The first is more-profile-row, with your photo in more-avatar, your account and the caption Profile, devices, sign out. The second holds the workspace switcher, Invitations, Agents, Admin for admins, and Get the iPhone app when offered. The workspace row ends with workspace-count, a --panel-hi pill with the number of saved workspaces in --text-2xs tabular digits. It hides when only one is saved, and the row's label reads the count to screen readers. The third card is Help & docs, with the build as its caption. The floating profile photo hides on More, since the first card replaces it. On phone, Profile ends with a more-card of Devices, IRC clients, and Sign out, the last as a mobile-row danger in danger ink. Pages opened from More or Profile sit at the bottom of the screen, just above the tab bar. .profile-screen > .mobile-screen-body::before is a flexible spacer, so a short page drops to thumb reach and a long one scrolls from the top. Do not add a mobile-spacer to these pages. Tab screens keep mobile-spacer. Phone screens scroll up and down only. .mobile-screen-body and .mobile-settings-body clip sideways overflow and stop the sideways rubber band (overflow-x: clip, overscroll-behavior-x: none), and on phones .chat and .reply-thread-stream do the same. Code blocks and tables that need the width scroll inside themselves. Anything wider than the screen is cut off rather than scrollable, so keep controls within their container. A hidden file input in a card takes sr-only, which the card's full-width input rule skips. On phone Home, DMs, More and in a conversation, pulling down from the very top shows pull-indicator (app/client/pull-refresh.ts), a glass chip under the header that holds pull-logo. The logo follows the finger with resistance, grows and turns as it goes, and stays grey until the pull goes past 64px, where it takes its color. A release past that point checks the connection and loads newer messages for the open conversation, with no page reload. The logo breathes while that runs, pops once when caught up and leaves with no text. Offline or unreachable widens the chip with pull-label: You're offline, or Couldn't reach Slirc. Reduced motion only fades. A pull that starts below the top, within 24px of either screen edge, or while a composer has focus stays a scroll, a back swipe or a keyboard drag. The chip sits at --z-pull-indicator (27). On phone, dragging down 24px or tapping the channel list or an open reply thread puts the keyboard away, but only while a composer has focus; taps on controls do nothing. In the iOS app and the Home Screen app, a swipe from the left 20px edge presses the back arrow on screen (reply-thread-back, then profile-back, then header .mobile-back). The page follows the finger and the swipe commits past 35% of the width or on a quick flick; reduced motion skips the slide. A screen with no back arrow ignores it, and text fields, open dialogs, sheets and sideways-scrolled code keep their own touches. A new phone screen with a back arrow uses one of those classes so the swipe finds it. Docs opened from the iOS app or a phone show app-back, a sticky Slirc bar above the docs top bar, which takes the notch inset and returns to the app. Its height is --app-back-h (2.5rem), set by docs-in-app; the docs top bar, sidebar and heading scroll offsets add it. On screens up to 640px the docs page clips sideways too, and inline code outside pre wraps anywhere, while code in tables stays on one line. The iOS app starts on its own workspace picker, native/www/index.html, with the same tokens. While it checks and opens a saved workspace, it shows opening: the slirc.org lockup pulsing at its center above Opening <host>…, with the pulse off under reduced motion. A workspace gets 5s to answer and 5s more for its client to start. A miss or a failed load brings back the picker with that workspace's card as card failed (a danger border at 55%) and a tag failed Couldn't reach pill where Current would be. A full-width Try again button sits above the form, and the field stays unfocused so the keyboard doesn't cover it. A cancelled load never opens the picker.

title: Design system
heading: Accessibility
text: Check text contrast against rendered backgrounds, including glass. Faint borders cannot be the only way to identify a control or keyboard focus. Label icon-only controls. Show keyboard focus with a solid accent outline. Dialogs keep Tab within visible, enabled controls. Escape cancels; closing returns focus to the opener. Preserve focus and text selection during rerenders. Keep fixed phone controls clear of safe-area insets. Use shortcode alt text for custom emoji. Show important state with text, icon, count, or position, not color alone. Honor reduced motion. Allow text selection when a mouse or other fine pointer is available.
